## One independently mergeable outcome

Connect four existing controlled transform checks to recorded world parameters, adding diagnostic per-world evidence to existing world certification reports. This is the bounded transform-only portion of the reviewed world-check feasibility proposal under the owner's existing continuous-development direction. Muse owns implementation choices; Codex independently reviews. Existing checks, tolerances, predicates, default CI/runtime behavior, certification levels and readiness meaning remain unchanged. The completed runner reliability task is the prerequisite; no new model family, numerical truth, threshold, policy, production or sibling capability is authorized.

## Inputs, preserved predicates and observable output

Read the ten existing WORLD-001 through WORLD-010 bundles and their world_truth.json as immutable inputs. Four checks are covered: geometric_adstock_carryover, hill_saturation_analytic, geometric_adstock_design_matrix, and hill_saturation_monotone_design_matrix. Use recorded per-channel decay for the two carryover checks and recorded per-channel Hill half/slope for the two Hill checks. Preserve the existing fixed impulse and zeroed comparator for design-matrix carryover; preserve the increasing spend grid for design-matrix monotonicity. Do not substitute arbitrary panel time sequences for those controlled comparisons. Preserve inherited exact closed-form tolerances (1e-12) and monotonicity tolerance (1e-9). Preserve the existing default values and other controlled parameters when only one transform parameter family is varied.

Maintain the single-source invariant: the new evaluator calls the same existing registry predicate implementation as zero-argument CI/runtime paths. Default-preserving keyword-only input extensions to these four check functions are permitted; their zero-argument outcomes, error meaning, predicates and thresholds remain unchanged. No duplicated predicate implementation, new check, or science is owned. Exact implementation design belongs to Muse.

Append one additive top-level world_exact_check_evaluations list to the existing report. One row per world/check, world lexical order then the existing registry order, with deterministic channel-name ordering. Each row records check_id and world_id strings, status pass or fail, expected and actual finite numbers or explanatory strings, tolerance finite number or null, message string, skip_reason null, evidence_refs mapping naming exact truth fields and values, and channels list of per-channel results with channel/expected/actual/status. A failure in any channel fails its row. Preserve all channel outcomes; do not hide simultaneous failures behind the summary. Summary values identify the binding channel deterministically, with lexical channel order resolving ties. The four checks on these ten worlds have no authorized inapplicability or skip case.

Missing or malformed truth, missing required fields, empty channels, nonfinite or invalid transform parameters fail affected rows with explicit reasons; do not silently skip, substitute defaults for missing world evidence, or certify it. Unsupported extra model families do not gain support. Existing report keys, validation_results, certification_level, production_readiness, overall acceptance logic, registry membership and report readers remain unchanged. Diagnostic rows do not become a new persistent certification gate; a failed required acceptance test blocks this task's publication. This additive report compatibility is tested against existing readers; no schema/data migration or fixture regeneration is authorized.
